# Incremental: exact re-checking in milliseconds

**Question:** after an edit, can the answer be updated exactly in milliseconds, instead of by a full check?
<!-- generated by tools/research/sync -->
**Stands:** On `warm-fingerprint-components-20261011-boolean`, the Mastodon edit confirms bounded reuse: fingerprint work falls 132.653 to 10.759 s, but fast warm excluding shadow is 23.901 s versus 7.349 s whole cold. On `replay-storage-support-20261011-storage-support`, 24 support rows pass while five of eight native storage cases lose reasons/order. These are one-pair shared-host profiles; exact fast replay remains open ([F37](../facts.md#f37), [F35](../facts.md#f35), [F34](../facts.md#f34), [F33](../facts.md#f33), [F30](../facts.md#f30), [F15](../facts.md#f15)).
**Skills:** Incremental computation; Rust performance; serialization.
**Claims:** none. To take this frontier, see [Claiming](../README.md#claiming).

## October 11 evidence

The [fingerprint component profile](https://github.com/bunnykong/roundhouse-fixpoint-lab/blob/509fdb324b451c73e7adc261693cb7298d550f52/receipts/warm-fingerprint-components-2026-10-11/README.md) confirms one bounded optimization with the old bytes, guards and replay order preserved ([F35](../facts.md#f35)). It still costs more than cold. The separate [native storage/support checks](https://github.com/bunnykong/roundhouse-fixpoint-lab/blob/509fdb324b451c73e7adc261693cb7298d550f52/receipts/replay-storage-support-2026-10-11/README.md) pass 24 support rows, reject an injected stale cycle and expose five payload fidelity losses ([F37](../facts.md#f37)). Preserve reason sets and ordered fields before codec reuse; full replay and mandatory shadow remain. The matrix does not certify complete components or dependencies ([F33](../facts.md#f33), [F34](../facts.md#f34)).

## Why it matters

Editors and agents re-check after every change. The pinned Discourse cold analyses take tens of seconds (F30), and the answer matters most while someone is typing.

## The check

The [October 10 profile receipt](https://github.com/bunnykong/roundhouse-fixpoint-lab/blob/d0b2e5dd689c04221295b9a4037dede07984c770/receipts/warm-profile-2026-10-10/README.md) pins the warm replay port
[`warm-next`](https://github.com/bunnykong/roundhouse/tree/warm-next) at `d9ec78c3` and retains the six frozen F15 edits.
Its runner verifies input trees, restores the same unedited seed before each replay, and checks
the mandatory shadow and a separate cold result. It records exclusive wall-time buckets,
whole command walls and the validation interval separately. These are profiles on a shared host,
with one cold-first timed pair per edit after a correctness replay, not benchmarks.

From a fresh lab clone:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/bunnykong/roundhouse-fixpoint-lab lab
cd lab
git checkout --detach d0b2e5dd689c04221295b9a4037dede07984c770
sh corpus/fetch.sh
python3 -B receipts/warm-profile-2026-10-10/rerun.py
python3 -B receipts/warm-profile-2026-10-10/recompute.py
```

The native rerun needs Python 3.9+, CRuby 4.0.7 with Prism, Rust 1.98.1 and native build dependencies.
Use `--binary FILE` for a prebuilt binary and `--lock FILE` for the host's shared analysis lock.
The offline reduction needs only Python and checks saved raw timing, parity and suite outputs.
The latency gate still requires every edit to match, five interleaved cost pairs and a warm path
well under a tenth of a second on Mastodon.

The earlier [`warm-edits`](../../../tools/research/warm-edits) recipe remains attached to
historical F15 on `fixpoint-warm`. Its analysis-only seconds exclude ingest and cache load/save;
they are distinct from F15's wall-time ratios and F30's phase profiles.

## Known

- By design, replay is exact when every read is recorded, transfers are monotone and writes are justified: replaying the stored records, then running the worklist to saturation, reaches the same fixpoint as a cold start. All six F30 body edits agree with the mandatory cold shadow and separate cold result; F37 adds a bounded support-deletion matrix, while complete component/read coverage remains open. The hypotheses aren't proved for the Rust analyzer.
- In F30, the unedited seeds load 60,698 records in 440.9 MiB of JSON on Mastodon and 136,952 records in 1,917.5 MiB on Discourse. F15’s older counts remain attached to its older compiler pin.
- Boolean edits replay over 98% of the surviving records.

## Leads

- F35 confirms bounded reuse of repeated canonical metadata. Replicate all six edits and five alternating pairs before broader speed claims; profile final hashing and class guards next, preserving bytes, generations and shadow.
- Store records per strongly connected component rather than per evaluation, and guard them with hashes.
- Replay only the components downstream of the edit.

## Read first

On `warm-next`: `src/analyze/warm.rs` (record, replay and shadow), `src/analyze/warm/fingerprint.rs`, `src/analyze/warm/wire.rs`, and the read recorder in `src/analyze/sccq.rs`.
